Wilbrink1#, Vanessa Herder1#, Kim Handrejk1#, Fabien Filaire1#, 4 Georgios Ilia2, Wai Wai Jones2, Luca M. Zaeck1, Debby van Eck Schipper1, Vincent P. Vaes1, 5 Sandhya Shrestha3, Johan Reimerink3, Laura L.A. van Dijk1, Mark Power1, Merel R. te Marvelde1, 6 Dennis de Meulder1, Hayley Cassidy1, Koen Wijnans1, Sharona Sacharoen–Rugebregt1, Alba 7 Grifoni4, Alessandro Sette4,5, Bas B. Oude Munink1, Chantal B.E.M. Reusken3,6, Bart L. 8 Haagmans1*, Rory D. de Vries1*, Sander Herfst1,7*, Massimo Palmarini 1,2* 9 10 1Department of Viroscience, Erasmus University Medical Center, Rotterdam, the Netherlands 11 2MRC-University of Glasgow Center for Virus Research, Glasgow, Scotland, United Kingdom 12 3Centre for Infectious Disease Control, National Institute for Public Health and the Environment 13 (RIVM), Bilthoven, the Netherlands. 14 4La Jolla Institute for Immunology, La Jolla, CA, USA 15 5Department of Medicine, University of California San Diego, La Jolla, CA, USA 16 6Virology group, Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Utrecht University, Utrecht, The Netherlands 17 7Pandemic and Disaster Preparedness Center, Delft, Rotterdam, The Netherlands. 18 19 #These authors contributed equally to this manuscript 20 *These senior authors contributed equally to this manuscript 21 Correspondence: m.palmarini@erasmusmc.nl 22 23 2 | P a g e Summary 24 In May 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) caused by Andes virus 25 (ANDV) was detected aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, sparking public health measures in 26 multiple countries. ANDV infections in humans are mostly sporadic, most often linked to exposure 27 to infected rodents in South America, although small clusters of human cases, like the 2026 28 outbreak on the MV Hondius occur as well. It is not known whether virological factors may 29 contribute to this distinct epidemiology, and no phenotypic characterization of the newly emerged 30 ANDV (ANDV2026) has been carried out to date. Here, using an ANDV isolate from a 31 presymptomatic patient from the MV Hondius, we studied pathogenesis, identified sites of viral 32 replication, characterized innate and adaptive immune responses, and quantified shedding in 33 golden Syrian hamsters. ANDV2026 proved to be highly pathogenic in hamsters, causing severe 34 pulmonary disease reminiscent of HPS. ANDV2026 triggered a delayed type-I IFN response and 35 inflammatory response in the lungs consistent with the key pathological features of HPS, and we 36 detected viral replication in both respiratory and extra-respiratory tissues, including the brain. 37 Infected animals mounted neutralizing antibodies and T cell responses, the latter directed 38 predominantly against the L and N proteins. Importantly, ANDV2026-infected animals shed virus 39 through multiple routes, and we detected infectious virus in air samplers connected to cages 40 housing ANDV2026-infected hamsters. In contrast, control hamsters infected with a rodent-derived 41 ANDV isolate (ANDV9717869) shed little virus and air samples were consistently negative. These 42 findings consolidate established features of ANDV pathogenesis, while revealing properties not 43 previously described. Phenotypic characterization of patient-derived ANDV isolates in animal 44 models can strengthen outbreak preparedness, identify markers of disease severity, and support 45 the development of medical countermeasures. 46 3 | P a g e INTRODUCTION 47 On the 2nd of May 2026, a cluster of severe respiratory disease aboard the Dutch cruise ship MV 48 Hondius was notified to the World Health organization (WHO)1-3. Soon after, ANDV was 49 diagnosed as the cause of the outbreak, which overall led to 13 reported cases, including three 50 deaths4. Confirmed cases were all aboard the MV Hondius, although the outbreak led to 51 monitoring of 653 individuals in 33 countries around the globe. 52 ANDV is classified within the family Orthohantaviridae5-8. These are viruses that cause two distinct 53 disease complexes: the hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Europe and Asia, and 54 the hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas, caused among others by Sin Nombre 55 virus (SNV) and Andes virus (ANDV), respectively9. HPS is usually presents in four distinct clinical 56 phases: febrile, cardiopulmonary, diuretic and convalescent10,11. Most cases are characterized by 57 pulmonary edema driven by increased vascular permeability, terminally leading to cardiogenic 58 shock and death12. The case fatality rate of the MV Hondius outbreak was 23%, lower than for 59 previously reported ANDV clusters. Direct comparison is difficult however, due to the relatively 60 low number of cases in this outbreak and early access to medical care for many of the individuals 61 affected13-15. 62 ANDV is endemic in Southern Argentina and Chile, where it causes seasonal outbreaks every 63 year9,16. Humans are believed to become infected mostly after exposure to aerosolized infectious 64 excretions of the rodent reservoir, the long-tailed rice rat (Oligoryzomys longicaudatus)5,6,17. 65 Andes virus (ANDV) was first detected in 1995, when it caused an outbreak of 16 cases and nine 66 deaths18. This outbreak and subsequent ones suggested that ANDV can be capable of human- 67 to-human transmission, with the main risk factor being in close contact with infected individuals in 68 enclosed settings18,19. Some cases have also been described without any documented direct 69 contact, hinting at a respiratory transmission route, though available data cannot distinguish 70 airborne shedding of infectious virus from contamination of the surrounding environment20. On 71 the MV Hondius, patients were in direct contact with each other, suggesting ANDV human-to- 72 4 | P a g e human transmission. One potential asymptomatic case of ANDV infection in a health-care worker 73 with low-level viraemia was also reported, despite only indirect exposure21-23. 74 Few studies have phenotyped ANDV isolates obtained directly from human patients21-23, and 75 fewer still have done so in vivo to define key viral characteristics such as virulence and host 76 responses22,24. This reflects the sporadic nature of HPS and its restricted geographical distribution. 77 ANDV is also notoriously difficult to isolate, as infection is typically diagnosed once patients have 78 already developed neutralizing antibodies. As a result, our understanding of the biological 79 differences between ANDV isolates associated with different cases and outbreaks is incomplete. 80 Here, we characterized the ANDV isolate associated with the MV Hondius outbreak 81 (ANDV/2026/hondius-NL-12, henceforth ANDV2026). Using the golden Syrian hamster model, we 82 studied viral pathogenesis, replication sites, and the host innate and adaptive immune responses. 83 We also analyzed virus shedding from infected animals and sampled air from the cages of infected 84 hamsters for ANDV RNA and infectious virus. Throughout our study, the human isolate ANDV2026 85 was compared with a rodent-derived ANDV strain (ANDV9717869). Altogether, in vivo phenotyping 86 contributes to the continuous risk assessment of emerging viruses of global health concern. 87 88 RESULTS 89 90 ANDV2026 causes severe, systemic infection in hamsters. Golden Syrian hamsters were 91 intranasally inoculated with a low dose (200 TCID50/hamster) of either ANDV2026 (n=18) or 92 ANDV9717869 (n=18). analysis.background: An outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) caused by Andes virus (ANDV) was detected aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius in May 2026, involving 13 cases and 3 deaths (23 % case‑fatality rate). ANDV infections are usually sporadic and linked to rodent exposure, but small human‑to‑human clusters such as this one have been reported.
analysis.methods: A patient‑derived ANDV isolate (ANDV2026) from a presymptomatic MV Hondius case was used to infect golden Syrian hamsters; a rodent‑derived ANDV isolate (ANDV9717869) served as control. Viral replication, immune responses, and shedding were assessed, including detection of infectious virus in air samplers connected to hamster cages.
analysis.results: ANDV2026 was highly pathogenic in hamsters, causing severe pulmonary disease. It induced a delayed type‑I IFN and inflammatory response, with viral replication in respiratory and extra‑respiratory tissues including brain. Infected animals mounted neutralising antibodies and T‑cell responses mainly against L and N proteins. ANDV2026 shed virus via multiple routes, and infectious virus was recovered from air samplers; control hamsters shed little virus and air samples were negative.
analysis.contribution: The study consolidates known features of ANDV pathogenesis and reveals previously undescribed properties, notably airborne shedding, thereby informing outbreak preparedness, identifying disease‑severity markers, and supporting medical countermeasure development.
analysis.limitations: not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: An outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome caused by Andes virus was detected aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius in May 2026, involving 13 cases and 3 deaths (23 % case‑fatality rate). Methods: A patient‑derived ANDV isolate (ANDV2026) was used to infect golden Syrian hamsters, with a rodent‑derived isolate (ANDV9717869) as control; viral replication, immune responses, and shedding—including air sampler detection—were assessed. Results: ANDV2026 was highly pathogenic, inducing delayed type‑I IFN and inflammatory responses, viral replication in respiratory and extra‑respiratory tissues, neutralising antibodies and T‑cell responses, and shedding of infectious virus into the air; control hamsters shed little virus. Contribution: The findings consolidate known ANDV pathogenesis features and reveal airborne shedding, informing outbreak preparedness and countermeasure development. Limitations: not reported in the supplied evidence.

papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis.
papers.abstract: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.

Supplementary Information The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1186/s44342-026-00081-8. Introduction Nephropathia epidemica (NE) is attributed to Puumala virus (PUUV), a naturally occurring form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in humans, which is a zoonotic infectious disease and generally considered a mild-to-moderate form of hantavirus infection within the HFRS spectrum. PUUV (Puumala orthohantavirus) is classified within the genus Orthohantavirus, family Hantaviridae, and order Bunyavirales, as defined by current ICTV taxonomy, and it was previously grouped under the family Bunyaviridae prior to taxonomic reclassification. PUUV infection presents with highly variable outcomes, ranging from subclinical cases (70–80%) to severe HFRS, and carries a fatality rate of about 0.1%. PUUV infection commonly presents with sudden fever, headache, back pain, nausea, gastrointestinal symptoms, thrombocytopenia, hematuria, and varying degrees of acute kidney impairment. In some patients, additional manifestations such as blurred vision, dizziness, insomnia, respiratory complications, oliguria, and subsequent polyuria during recovery may also occur. Although PUUV infection is generally considered mild, severe complications can occur in a subset of patients, including acute kidney failure, hypotension, shock, pulmonary edema, Guillain-Barré syndrome, respiratory distress, disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC), myocarditis, encephalitis, pituitary hemorrhage, seizures, and, in rare cases, multiorgan failure or fatal cerebral hemorrhage. The first identification of PUUV occurred in the early 1980s when the virus was isolated from bank voles (Myodes glareolus) in the Puumala region of Finland. Between July 1989 and June 1996, Finland reported 6701 PUUV infection cases confirmed via serological assays, with the highest incidence in the Itä-Savo district and a mortality rate below 0.1%, and later from 1995 to 2008, 22,681 cases were recorded with an average annual incidence of 31 per 100,000 population, resulting in 13 deaths and 52% of patients requiring hospitalization. PUUV accounts for approximately 93% of all notified hantavirus infections in Germany and caused a major outbreak in 2007 in Baden-Württemberg with 1089 reported human cases, while the highest annual number of PUUV infections in Germany was recorded in 2010 since hantavirus surveillance began in 2001. Also in 2007, Sweden’s Västerbotten County experienced a surprisingly severe outbreak of PUUV infection, with NE rates hitting 313 cases per 100,000 residents. Between 2001 and 2017, a total of 12,148 hantavirus disease cases were recorded, of which 9714 (approximately 97.41%) were attributed to PUUV infection. In 2019, Europe recorded over 4000 hantavirus cases (0.8 per 100,000), 98% caused by PUUV, with Finland and Germany making up 69% of the total. From 2018 to 2025, Hungary recorded 51 lab-confirmed hantavirus infections, 20 of which were specifically linked to the PUUV. In Finland, between 560 and 3800 cases of NE are reported each year, though the actual number is believed to be nearly six times higher. PUUV is a spherical enveloped pathogen characterized by a segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome. The PUUV possesses a tripartite genome: the L segment (~ 6.5 kb) encodes a ~ 2156-amino-acid L protein (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with replicase, transcriptase, and endonuclease functions; the M segment (~ 3.7 kb) encodes a ~ 1148-amino-acid glycoprotein precursor that is co-translationally cleaved into Gn (70 kDa) and Gc (55 kDa); and the S segment (~ 1.8 kb) encodes a ~ 433-amino-acid nucleocapsid (N) protein. Gc is the protein that mediates fusion by the identification of a peptide of fusion, whereas Gn serves as a folding chaperone for Gc and controls the time of fusion; both are necessary for the virus to adhere as well as enter host cells. Gn and Gc form the principal antigenic surface of PUUV and are major targets of neutralizing antibodies, contributing to protective immunity and vaccine relevance. The N protein plays multiple roles in viral genome transport, replication, and assembly through its interactions with host cellular proteins, while also acting as a highly immunogenic viral component in both humans and animal models. The N protein is highly conserved among orthohantaviruses and elicits a strong early antibody response during acute infection, making it an important target for both diagnostic applications and vaccine development. Various vaccine platforms are available, each possessing distinct advantages and drawbacks. For example, live attenuated vaccines trigger strong, long-lasting immunity but can be risky for immunocompromised individuals due to possible reversion to virulence; inactivated vaccines are safer and more stable, though they usually require multiple doses; subunit vaccines use only key antigens, lowering the chance of side effects, but often need adjuvants and booster shots to achieve durable protection. Moreover, DNA vaccines offer rapid, stable, and cost-effective production with long-lasting immunity, but they often show weak immunogenicity in humans and face delivery challenges. In contrast, the key advantage of mRNA vaccines lies in their rapid design and production, enabling swift responses to emerging infections and pandemic threats without the need to culture live pathogens. In recognition of these advances, the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honored Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for their groundbreaking contributions to nucleoside engineering, a key innovation that enabled the successful development of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19. Recent developments in bioinformatics have improved biopharmaceutical design by enabling rapid prediction of protein features, structural modeling, and immunogenicity assessment. These computational approaches accelerate the identification and optimization of therapeutic candidates while reducing time and experimental costs; however, challenges related to prediction accuracy, biological complexity, and the need for experimental validation remain important considerations. Reverse vaccinology (RV) applies bioinformatics and immunoinformatics to screen microbial genomes for conserved, immunogenic epitopes, enabling faster, safer, and cost-effective vaccine development compared to traditional pathogen culturing, a slow and labor-intensive process. Vaccine development against PUUV infection has included inactivated whole-virus vaccines, recombinant subunit vaccines, virus-like particle (VLP)-based approaches, and DNA vaccines. Among these, inactivated and DNA vaccine candidates have demonstrated promising immunogenicity in preclinical studies. Currently, no vaccine has been authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for PUUV infection. Several studies have suggested the potential of multi-epitope vaccine approaches using immunoinformatics-based strategies. Khan et al. developed a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against SARS-CoV-2 by integrating epitope prediction, antigenicity assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response analysis, demonstrating the feasibility of computational vaccine design approaches. Similarly, Peele et al. designed a multi-epitope vaccine construct containing predicted B-cell and T-cell epitopes and evaluated its structural and immunological properties through computational analyses. These studies highlighted the potential of combining multiple immune targets within a single vaccine construct; however, their findings remained primarily dependent on computational predictions and required experimental validation to confirm immunogenicity and protective efficacy. However, despite these advances, several challenges remain in current multi-epitope vaccine development strategies. Computational vaccine designs are dependent on prediction algorithms, reference databases, structural modeling assumptions, and available biological information, which may influence the reliability of predicted vaccine candidates. In addition, variations in epitope selection criteria, antigen conservation analysis, population coverage evaluation, and structural validation approaches can affect the effectiveness of computational vaccine design. Recent studies have emphasized that although immunoinformatics approaches accelerate multi-epitope vaccine development, comprehensive experimental validation remains essential for confirming biological relevance and protective potential. Despite previous vaccine development efforts, including inactivated whole-virus vaccines, recombinant subunit vaccines, virus-like particle (VLP)-based approaches, and DNA vaccine candidates, no PUUV vaccine has currently received regulatory approval. An integrated mRNA multi-epitope vaccine strategy targeting conserved regions of both PUUV glycoproteins (Gn/Gc) and nucleocapsid protein remains insufficiently explored. A comprehensive framework combining conserved antigen identification, multi-epitope vaccine construction, structural evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response prediction for PUUV has not been extensively investigated. Therefore, this study aimed to design and evaluate the PV-GNProtecta vaccine candidate using an integrated immunoinformatics workflow involving conserved antigen identification, epitope prediction, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response prediction. The findings provide computational insights into the potential characteristics of PV-GNProtecta while recognizing the necessity of experimental validation for future assessment. Materials and methods Acquisition and characterization of viral protein sequences The UniProt protein database (https://www.uniprot.org/; accessed on 15 July 2025) was used for obtaining amino acid sequences of the target proteins from PUUV of G (accession number: P41266) and N (accession numbers: P41270). The G and N proteins were selected due to their key roles in PUUV infection and immune recognition. The G protein mediates viral attachment and entry and is a major target of neutralizing antibodies, whereas the highly conserved N protein contributes to viral replication and induces strong immune responses. Compared with the intracellular RdRp/L protein, G and N provide more suitable targets for antibody and cellular immune responses. A comparative evaluation of these proteins is provided in Supplementary Table S14. Physicochemical and structural characterization of selected proteins The selected PUUV G and N proteins were characterized for signal peptide presence, transmembrane regions, and subcellular localization. Signal peptide prediction was performed using SignalP 6.0 (https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/services/SignalP-6.0/; accessed on 15 September 2026) with the organism group selected as Eukarya and the default prediction model. Transmembrane topology was predicted using DeepTMHMM version 1.0.57 (accessed on 15 September 2026) using the default settings. Subcellular localization information was obtained from UniProt (https://www.uniprot.org/; accessed on 15 September 2026) based on available curated annotations. Analysis of multiple sequence alignment and evolutionary relationships To support RV analysis, the sequence is encoded using amino acid residue codes and preserved as a FASTA sequence file. The acquired sequences were subsequently utilized for multiple sequence alignment (MSA) through the Clustal Omega platform (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/jdispatcher/msa/clustalo; accessed on 05 August 2025). The Mega X tool (https://www.megasoftware.net/; accessed on 05 August 2025) was employed for phylogenetic analysis on both genomes. Prediction of epitopes for MHC I, MHC II, and linear B-cell interactions The MHC I epitopes from the G and N proteins were found using the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) (http://tools.iedb.org/mhci/; accessed on 20 August 2025) software, with a percentile rank < 1.00 as the selection criterion. This tool is a sophisticated database comprising information on MHC molecules, T-cell and B-cell epitopes, antibodies, and MHC-binding ligands identified in humans and various animal taxonomic groups, including primates and rodents. A cutoff percentile rank of less than 1.00 was implemented for epitope selection, which suggests that the binding affinity was improved. Lower percentile rank values indicate stronger predicted peptide–MHC binding affinity. The IEDB (http://tools.iedb.org/mhcii/; accessed on 20 August 2025) was applied to forecast the MHC II epitopes inside the designated areas of these proteins, and peptides with percentile ranks < 1.00 were considered potential high-affinity binders and selected for further evaluation. Subsequently, the human allele reference sets were employed to predict CD8 + and CD4 + binding. The ABCpred tool (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/abcpred/; accessed on 25 August 2025) was used to estimate the continuous B-cell epitopes of the selected portions of these proteins. This tool provides epitope predictions by analyzing the sequence features of the target antigens. This program uses an affinity scale method based on a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to predict continuous B-cell epitopes. Additionally, the MHC-II epitopes underwent some additional analyses, including IL-10 (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/il10pred/; accessed on 25 September 2026), IFN-gamma (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/ifnepitope/predict.php; accessed on 25 September 2026), IL-2 (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/il2pred/; accessed on 25 September 2026) and IL-4 (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/il4pred/design.php; accessed on 25 September 2026) by using the respective servers. Linear B-cell epitopes were forecasted with ABCpred with a standard window length of 16 amino acids and a score cutoff of 0.51. Antigenicity was evaluated using the VaxiJen v2.0 (https://www.ddg-pharmfac.net/vaxijen/VaxiJen/VaxiJen.html; accessed on 28 August 2025) server under the viral protein model with the default threshold value of 0.4. Peptides with antigenicity scores ≥ 0.4 were considered probable antigens and retained for further analysis, whereas those scoring below this threshold were excluded. The threshold value of 0.4 was selected based on the default classification cutoff recommended for the VaxiJen viral model, which was established through performance evaluation of the prediction system. AllerTOP v2.1 (threshold: 0.5) (https://www.ddg-pharmfac.net/allertop_test/; accessed on 28 August 2025) and ToxinPred (threshold: 0.0) servers (https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/toxinpred/algo.php; accessed on 28 August 2025) were deployed in order to make predictions on allergenicity and toxicity, respectively. The allergenicity was evaluated utilizing AllerTOP v2.1 with the server's standard ACC/k-NN algorithm configurations. Also, toxicity prediction was performed using the ToxinPred server with the SVM (Swiss-Prot)-based prediction method, applying the default threshold value of 0.0 and a window length of 17 residues. Peptides were classified according to the server-generated SVM prediction score, and sequences predicted as toxic were excluded, whereas non-toxic peptides were retained for further analysis. All settings were preserved according to the server’s default configuration. The selected epitopes were not chosen based only on prediction scores; additional analyses, including antigenicity, safety assessment, sequence conservation, population coverage, and MHC interaction evaluation, were also considered to improve the reliability of epitope selection. Evaluation of population-level coverage The prevalence of HLA alleles varies across different geographies and ethnic communities. analysis.background: Puumala virus (PUUV) is the main cause of nephropathia epidemica, a zoonotic disease with renal complications and no approved vaccine, representing a public‑health threat.
analysis.methods: An immunoinformatics‑driven approach was used to design an mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine (PV‑GNProtecta) from conserved glycoprotein G and nucleoprotein N regions; epitope prediction, antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, population‑coverage, physicochemical and structural modeling, docking, MM‑GBSA, 100 ns molecular dynamics, codon optimization for E. coli, and immune‑simulation were performed in silico. Location/host details are not reported in the supplied evidence.
analysis.results: Highly antigenic, non‑allergenic, non‑toxic T‑ and B‑cell epitopes were identified; population‑coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness; the construct showed favorable stability, solubility and antigenicity; structural validation reported 95.5 % residues in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4; docking and MM‑GBSA predicted strong interaction with TLR4, supported by a 100 ns MD simulation; codon optimization indicated compatibility with E. coli expression; immune simulation predicted increased IgG, IFN‑γ and IL‑2 levels.
analysis.contribution: The study provides a computationally validated mRNA vaccine candidate and demonstrates broad HLA coverage and strong predicted immunogenicity, offering a basis for further experimental PUUV vaccine development.
analysis.limitations: All results are based on in silico analyses; experimental validation of translational efficiency, stability, expression, and immunogenicity is required; no laboratory or clinical data are presented.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Puumala virus causes nephropathia epidemica, a zoonotic disease with renal complications and no approved vaccine. Methods: An immunoinformatics pipeline designed an mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine (PV‑GNProtecta) using conserved G and N regions, with epitope prediction, population coverage, structural modeling, docking, MD simulation, codon optimization, and immune simulation performed in silico. Results: The vaccine contains highly antigenic, non‑allergenic, non‑toxic epitopes, shows broad HLA coverage, favorable physicochemical properties, 95.5 % Ramachandran‑favored residues, ERRAT 91.4, strong predicted TLR4 interaction, and simulated IgG, IFN‑γ, IL‑2 responses. Contribution: Offers a computationally validated mRNA vaccine candidate that may accelerate PUUV vaccine research. Limitations: Findings are limited to computational predictions; experimental validation is needed.

analysis_zh.methods: 采用免疫信息学驱动的方法,从保守的糖蛋白G和核蛋白N区域设计了mRNA多表位疫苗(PV‐GNProtecta);在体外进行表位预测、抗原性、致敏性、毒性、群体覆盖率、理化及结构建模、对接、MM‐GBSA、100 ns分子动力学、针对大肠杆菌的密码子优化以及免疫模拟。提供的证据中未报告位置/宿主信息。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究提供了经计算验证的mRNA疫苗候选方案,展示了广泛的HLA覆盖和强预测免疫原性,为进一步实验性PUUV疫苗研发奠定基础。
analysis_zh.limitations: 所有结果均基于体外计算分析;需进行翻译效率、稳定性、表达及免疫原性的实验验证;未提供实验室或临床数据。

papers.title: Human febrile illness associated with Yanggou tick virus: Clinical characteristics and epidemiological links to rodents.
papers.abstract: Objectives We identified Yanggou tick virus (YGTV), a segmented flavivirus previously unrecognized as a human pathogen, in a patient presenting with fever and headache. This study aims to characterize the epidemiology and clinical manifestations of YGTV infection in patients with fever of unknown origin (FUO). Methods We conducted a surveillance study at the First Hospital of Jilin University (2020-2025) involving 1011 patients with FUO. Concurrently, ticks and rodents in the vicinity of the patients' residences and workplaces were collected for viral detection. YGTV infection was confirmed via PCR assays. Positive samples were used for viral isolation, genome amplification, and phylogenetic characterization. An Apodemus agrarius challenge model was established to evaluate viral persistence and shedding. Results Of the 30 confirmed cases of YGTV infection, 10 were co-diagnosed with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). The patients showed no clear seasonality or geographic bias. Notably, rodent contact (43.3%) was a more frequent risk factor than tick bites (6.7%). While clinical presentations were non-specific, nearly 50% of the patients presented with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms. YGTV was isolated from patients, ticks, and A. agrarius (the latter often co-infected with Hantaan virus). Animal models confirmed persistent splenic infection and viral shedding via oral and fecal routes. Conclusion Our findings establish YGTV as an underdiagnosed cause of human febrile illness, underscoring the transmission risks posed by tick vectors and rodent reservoirs. These results highlight the urgent need for enhanced clinical surveillance and diagnostic screening among patients presenting with FUO, particularly in regions where the virus is endemic.

analysis.background: YGTV, a segmented flavivirus previously unrecognized as a human pathogen, was identified in a patient presenting with fever and headache (A1).
analysis.methods: A surveillance study (2020‑2025) of 1011 FUO patients at the First Hospital of Jilin University used PCR to confirm YGTV infection (A3, A5); ticks and rodents near patients' homes were collected for viral detection (A4); positive samples underwent isolation, genome amplification, and phylogenetic analysis (A6); an Apodemus agrarius challenge model evaluated viral persistence and shedding (A7).
analysis.results: Thirty YGTV cases were confirmed, including 10 co‑diagnosed with HFRS (A8); cases showed no clear seasonality or geographic bias (A9); rodent contact (43.3%) was more common than tick bites (6.7%) (A10); ~50% had gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms (A11); YGTV was isolated from patients, ticks, and A. agrarius (often co‑infected with Hantaan virus) (A12‑A13); animal models demonstrated persistent splenic infection and oral/fecal shedding (A14).
analysis.contribution: The study establishes YGTV as an underdiagnosed cause of human febrile illness, emphasizing transmission risks from ticks and rodents and urging enhanced clinical surveillance and diagnostic screening in endemic areas (A15‑A16).
analysis.limitations: Only abstract data are provided; detailed methodology, sample‑size breakdowns, and statistical analyses are not reported (abstract_only).

analysis.summary_en: Background: YGTV, a segmented flavivirus previously unrecognized as a human pathogen, was identified in a patient with fever and headache. Methods: A surveillance study (2020‑2025) of 1011 FUO patients used PCR for YGTV detection, collected ticks and rodents near residences, performed viral isolation and phylogenetic analysis, and used an Apodemus agrarius model to assess persistence. Results: Thirty cases were confirmed (10 co‑diagnosed with HFRS); no seasonality or geographic bias; rodent contact (43.3%) exceeded tick bites (6.7%); ~50% had gastrointestinal/neurological symptoms; YGTV isolated from patients, ticks, and rodents; animal models showed splenic persistence and oral/fecal shedding. Contribution: Establishes YGTV as an underdiagnosed febrile illness agent, highlighting tick and rodent transmission and the need for improved surveillance and diagnostics. Limitations: Only abstract data are available; detailed methods and analyses are not reported.

papers.title_zh: 与羊沟蜱病毒相关的人类发热疾病:临床特征及与啮齿动物的流行病学关联

analysis_zh.background: YGTV,一种先前未被认定为人类病原体的分段黄病毒,在一例出现发热和头痛的患者中被鉴定(A1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 在吉林大学第一医院对1011例发热原因不明(FUO)患者进行的2020‐2025年监测研究中,使用PCR确认YGTV感染(A3, A5);在患者居住附近采集蜱虫和啮齿动物用于病毒检测(A4);阳性样本进行分离、基因组扩增和系统发育分析(A6);采用Apodemus agrarius挑战模型评估病毒的持续感染和排泄(A7)。
analysis_zh.results: 确认了30例YGTV感染,其中10例合并诊断为HFRS(A8);病例未显示明显的季节性或地域偏好(A9);与啮齿动物接触(43.3%)的比例高于蜱虫叮咬(6.7%)(A10);约50%出现胃肠道和神经系统症状(A11);YGTV已从患者、蜱虫和A. agrarius中分离(常与汉滩病毒共感染)(A12‐A13);动物模型显示脾脏持续感染并通过口腔/粪便排泄(A14)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究确认YGTV是人类发热疾病的未被充分诊断的病因,强调蜱虫和啮齿动物的传播风险,并呼吁在流行地区加强临床监测和诊断筛查(A15‐A16)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要数据;未报告详细方法、样本量分布及统计分析(abstract_only)。

papers.title: Hantavirus in Dentistry: Occupational Exposure Considerations and a Proposed Tiered Infection Prevention and Control Framework-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Objective The aim of this study is to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry, and to propose an evidence-informed tiered infection prevention and control (IPC) framework that distinguishes established from theoretical risk. Material and methods The initial narrative search covered database inception through May 15, 2026 in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and WHO/CDC/ECDC/OSHA sources, followed by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and public-health guidance update through August 18, 2026. Approximately 1450 records were identified. After duplicate removal, 1070 records were subjected to title/abstract screening, 215 full-text records were assessed for eligibility, and 45 sources were included in the final synthesis, comprising 34 peer-reviewed publications and 11 gray-literature or public-health guidance sources. Results Environmental exposure to infected-rodent contamination is the established occupational pathway. Limited person-to-person transmission is documented for the Andes virus (ANDV), but no dental transmission has been reported. ANDV RNA and culture-based infectivity have been demonstrated in some oral/respiratory fluids; however, dental-aerosol transmission has not been shown. Dental-specific occupational risk therefore remains unquantified. Conclusions No dental transmission has been documented, and patient-related risk remains uncertain. Standard precautions and rodent control are foundational; suspected or confirmed ANDV warrants transmission-based precautions and airborne precautions for aerosol-generating procedures according to current guidance. The proposed dental tiers are evidence-informed, author-derived, and unvalidated.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 在牙科:职业暴露考虑及提出的分层感染预防与控制框架——叙述性综述。

analysis_zh.background: 本综述旨在综合关于汉坦病毒传播途径及与牙科实践相关的职业暴露证据。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 概述环境啮齿动物暴露为主要已确认途径,指出安第斯病毒的人际传播有限,并提出针对牙科环境的分层感染预防措施。
analysis_zh.current_state: 证据显示尚未记录汉坦病毒的牙科传播,仅有极少数安第斯病毒的人际病例,且患者相关风险尚不确定。
analysis_zh.gaps: 牙科特定职业风险的规模尚未量化,所提出的分层框架缺乏实证验证。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要开展分层感染控制框架的验证研究,以及对牙科操作中汉坦病毒暴露风险的定量评估。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：本综述旨在综合关于汉坦病毒传播途径及与牙科实践相关的职业暴露证据。 主要方向：概述环境啮齿动物暴露为主要已确认途径,指出安第斯病毒的人际传播有限,并提出针对牙科环境的分层感染预防措施。 研究现状：证据显示尚未记录汉坦病毒的牙科传播,仅有极少数安第斯病毒的人际病例,且患者相关风险尚不确定。 不足：牙科特定职业风险的规模尚未量化,所提出的分层框架缺乏实证验证。 后续研究：需要开展分层感染控制框架的验证研究,以及对牙科操作中汉坦病毒暴露风险的定量评估。

papers.title: DNA and mRNA Vaccines Against Hantaviruses: Antigen Design, Delivery Strategies and Translational Progress.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are members of the Hantaviridae family, which can cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). At present, no specific antiviral treatment is available for hantavirus infection, while licensed hantavirus vaccines are restricted to a limited number of countries in Asia. This review summarizes recent advances in hantavirus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines, focusing on antigen design, delivery systems, immunogenicity, safety and translational development. Peer-reviewed studies published primarily within the past 10 years were evaluated together with available hantavirus vaccine trials registered in ClinicalTrials.gov, with emphasis on Hantaan virus (HTNV), Puumala virus (PUUV) and Andes virus (ANDV). DNA vaccine candidates have demonstrated immunogenicity in preclinical and early clinical studies, with an acceptable safety profile. mRNA vaccines represent a newer approach with promising preclinical evidence of humoral and cellular immune responses. However, they have not yet been evaluated clinically. Studies have also reported the potential for varying degrees of cross-protection between hantavirus species, although protection remains limited by antigenic diversity. Overall, current evidence supports further development of nucleic acid-based hantavirus vaccines, particularly multivalent strategies, with emphasis on standardized evaluation and clinical efficacy.

papers.title: Epidemiology and Economic Burden of Puumala Virus Infection in Styria, Austria, 2003 to 2024.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and impose a potential burden on healthcare systems. However, comprehensive economic data remain scarce. We quantified the inpatient economic burden of hospitalized patients with Puumala virus (PUUV) infections in Styria, Austria's primary endemic region, to identify hospitalization costs and early admission predictors of costs. METHODS: This retrospective cost-of-illness study analyzed 1049 serologically confirmed PUUV hospitalizations across 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria between September 2003 and March 2024. Costs were estimated using the Austrian performance-oriented hospital financing (Leistungsorientierte Krankenanstaltenfinanzierung) diagnosis-related group system, standardized to 2024-equivalent Euros using consumer price index deflation. Admission predictors of cost were assessed using multivariable γ-generalized linear modeling with multiple imputations. Temporal trends in length of stay were analyzed using weighted segmented linear regression. RESULTS: Cumulative inpatient cost was ∼€10.3 million (mean per-case: €9788) for the entire study period of 21 years. Three epidemic years (2012, 2019, and 2021) accounted for 53.6% of cases and over €5.2 million in expenditure, with peak annual costs reaching €1.93 million (0.274% of total Styrian inpatient expenditure) in 2012. Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; cost-ratio 1.024 per second, 95% CI 1.019-1.030) and older age (CR 1.004 per year, 95% CI 1.001-1.008) were independent admission-level predictors of higher cost. Median hospital length of stay declined by ∼50% over the study period. CONCLUSIONS: PUUV hospitalizations impose a sharply episodic but recurrent economic burden on regional healthcare systems. Admission aPTT and age independently predicted cost, but clinical outcomes were not modeled and these variables do not constitute a triage tool. Epidemic preparedness strategies are warranted.

papers.title_zh: 2003至2024年奥地利施蒂利亚地区 普马拉病毒 感染的流行病学与经济负担。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒感染导致肾综合征出血热,并对医疗系统构成潜在负担。
analysis_zh.methods: 回顾性费用-疾病负担研究分析了2003年9月至2024年3月期间奥地利斯蒂里亚地区20家公立医院中1,049例血清学确诊的普马拉病毒住院病例;费用采用奥地利以绩效为导向的医院融资诊断相关组系统,标准化为2024欧元进行估算,入院费用预测因素通过多变量γ广义线性模型并结合多重插补进行评估;住院时长的时间趋势使用加权分段线性回归分析。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究量化了普马拉病毒住院对区域医疗系统的间歇性但反复出现的经济负担,并识别出费用预测因素,为流行病防备策略提供参考。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未对临床结局进行建模,且预测因素并不构成分诊工具;仅有摘要数据可用。

papers.title: Seasonal Dynamics, Host Network Structure, and Environmental Drivers of Gamasid Mite Communities on Small Mammals in a Dry-Hot Valley: A Year-Round Monitoring Study.
papers.abstract: Ectoparasitic gamasid mites on small mammals play crucial roles in transmitting zoonotic pathogens like hantaviruses associated with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). To elucidate their community, network structure, and seasonal drivers in xeric habitats, a consecutive 12-month localized survey was conducted in Waxi Village, Binchuan County, a dry-hot valley in Yunnan Province, southwest China, from November 2020 to October 2021. From 1329 captured small mammals (18 species, 89.62% rodents), 12,075 gamasid mites belonging to 33 species were identified. The community exhibited overwhelming dominance by the family Laelapidae (Cr = 99.35%) and genus Laelaps (Cr = 97.37%). Laelaps algericus, L. guizhouensis, and L. nuttalli constituted the dominant mite species (cumulative Cr = 88.96%) and formed a tightly correlated core species cluster. Overall infestation prevalence (PM), mean intensity (MI), and mean abundance (MA) were 46.05%, 19.73 mites/host, and 9.09 mites/host, respectively. The bipartite host-gamasid network revealed a significantly nested architecture (NODFobs = 31.16, Z = 14.03, p < 0.001) with high specialization (H2' = 0.599), anchored by dominant hosts (Rattus andamanensis, Apodemus chevrieri, and Mus caroli). α-diversity analysis showed that Margalef richness, Shannon-Wiener index, and Gini-Simpson index peaked in autumn (November), while troughs occurred in mid-spring (April) and mid-autumn (October). Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS, stress = 0.0048) and PERMANOVA (R2 = 0.074, p = 0.001) confirmed significant seasonal shifts in community composition. Standard redundancy analysis (RDA) suggested temperature as the primary climatic driver (F = 7.205, p = 0.001; total model explanation = 8.2%). However, partial RDA (pRDA) conditioning on host species identity demonstrated that climatic variables directly accounted for only 0.1% of net variance (F = 0.662, p = 0.521). Our findings indicate that gamasid mite community assembly in this dry-hot valley is characterized by strong species dominance and network nestedness and that seasonal fluctuations are consistent with a host-mediated pattern rather than being directly governed by climate.

analysis_zh.background: 小型哺乳动物的外寄生伽马螨是汉坦病毒等人畜共患病原体的重要媒介,导致肾综合征出血热。
analysis_zh.methods: 在云南省宾川县瓦溪村进行为期12个月的局部调查,捕获1,329只小型哺乳动物(18个物种),鉴定出33个物种的12,075只伽马螨。
analysis_zh.results: 蜱科(Laelapidae)占优势(Cr = 99.35%),其中Laelaps属(Cr = 97.37%)占螨类的88.96%;总体寄生率为46.05%,平均强度为19.73只螨/宿主,平均丰度为9.09。网络分析显示嵌套结构(NODFobs = 31.16,Z = 14.03,p < 0.001)和高专化度(H2′ = 0.599)。α多样性在秋季达到峰值;NMDS和PERMANOVA证实季节性变化;RDA表明温度是主要气候驱动因素(F = 7.205,p = 0.001,解释变异8.2%),但在控制宿主身份后,部分RDA显示气候仅解释0.1%。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究结果显示物种优势显著,网络呈嵌套结构,季节动态主要由宿主介导而非直接受气候控制,为人畜共患风险监测提供参考。

papers.title: [Nucleoside analogues in etiotropic therapy of hantavirus fevers].
papers.abstract: Hantavirus fevers (HF) are caused by pathogenic orthohantaviruses and are classified into two clinical forms: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), reported in Eurasia, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), reported in the Americas. HF are characterised by an acute course with predominant involvement of internal organs: HFRS is mainly associated with kidney damage, while HPS is characterised by severe lung injury. Both diseases may also affect the central nervous and endocrine systems. In addition, hantavirus fevers are marked by severe complications during the acute phase and a prolonged recovery period. Currently, there is neither a WHO-approved vaccine nor any effective etiotropic anti-hantavirus therapy. The development of antiviral treatment strategies focuses on preventing orthohantavirus entry into cells or suppressing their intracellular replication. One of the main directions in the search for effective anti-hantavirus therapy is the low-molecular-weight compounds development and testing, many of which have demonstrated pronounced antiviral activity against orthohantaviruses through direct or indirect effects on viral RNA polymerase function. The review shows that new antiviral nucleoside compounds development and study has promising potential, as well as their combined use for effective etiotropic, pathogenetic and symptomatic treatment of hantavirus fevers.

papers.title: Andes virus aboard the MV Hondius: Transnational public health challenges in ocean-going cruise travel
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the cluster of Andes virus infections that occurred aboard the expedition vessel MV Hondius during a transatlantic crossing. Drawing on publicly available information released by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, it examines the key characteristics of this event: probable exposure in a natural reservoir area in South America before embarkation, limited human-to-human transmission in a closed maritime environment, difficulties in early case recognition, and the complexity of international contact tracing. The analysis shows that the vessel itself was not the source of the virus, but rather a setting in which public health risks were amplified due to prolonged cohabitation, limited onboard medical resources, and the cross-border mobility of passengers. Finally, the article highlights the importance of stratified contact management, timely reporting, effective international cooperation, and clear risk communication to avoid both underestimation of the risk and unnecessary public panic.

papers.title_zh: 安第斯病毒 在 MV Hondius 号上:跨国公共卫生挑战在远洋邮轮旅行中的表现

analysis_zh.background: 本文分析了在跨大西洋航行期间,探险船 MV Hondius 上发生的 安第斯病毒 感染聚集事件。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者利用世卫组织、欧洲疾病预防控制中心和美国疾病控制中心的公开信息,审查了登船前在南美储宿动物中的可能暴露、船上有限的人际传播、早期病例识别困难以及国际接触者追踪的复杂性。
analysis_zh.results: 分析表明该船并非 安第斯病毒 的来源;相反,船舶环境因长期同居、船上医疗资源有限以及跨境乘客流动而放大了风险。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本文强调分层接触管理、及时报告、有效的国际合作以及明确的风险沟通的重要性,以避免风险低估和不必要的公众恐慌。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要,导致方法、定量数据和病例数的细节受限。
